visual_logic: Isolates a single, delicate avialan tooth to highlight the recurved 'catch and hold' predatory adaptations of early transitional theropods.
prompt: Extreme macro high-fidelity 3D asset render of a single fossilized tooth from an Archaeopteryx, capturing its specialized predatory morphology in a 3D animated feature film aesthetic. The tooth is miniature and delicate, shaped like a sharply backward-curved (recurved) hook. The texture is a translucent, fossilized ivory with microscopic, razor-sharp serrations clearly defined along the inner concave cutting edge. The single tooth is isolated and oriented vertically, centered perfectly on a 1:1 square canvas. High-key studio lighting with precise ambient occlusion emphasizes the fine serrated detail and the elegant hook silhouette. The background is a seamless, solid light-grey studio plane extending completely to the canvas margins with no internal borders or containment boxes. The object is scaled to ensure a strict 25% empty background framing buffer on all four sides to eliminate UI clipping. Grounded flat with realistic contact shadows. A tiny, clean checkered black-and-white scientific scale bar sits centered at the bottom.
